exposure: intrauterine transfusion before 18 weeks of gestation
localisation of needle insertion (intra-abdominal or placental)
outcome: premature delivery within seven days of procedure
abnormal fetal heart rate indicating emergency cesarean section within 24 hours of procedure
in utero death related to procedure
cohort: The study included 37 fetuses who underwent 86 intrauterine transfusions between 2001 and 2017 due to erythrocyte allo-immunization.
finding: The overall survival rate was 88.9% with a severe complication rate of 5.8% per intrauterine transfusion, and early procedures (before 18 weeks of gestation) were associated with a higher rate of complications.
followup_time: Up to neonatal death, with immediate procedure-related complications observed within 7 days or 24 hours.
gest_age: Intervention timing was specifically studied for gestational age before 18 weeks, with complications observed at various gestational ages during the study period (2001-2017).
